r=subprocess.run(['nvcc','-O3','--use_fast_math','-std=c++17','-cubin','-Xptxas','-v','-gencode','arch=compute_100a,code=sm_100a','-o','/tmp/e3p/f.cubin','/tmp/e3p/full.cu'],capture_output=True,text=True)
print(r.stdout[-3000:], r.stderr[-3000:])
r=subprocess.run(['cuobjdump','-sass','/tmp/e3p/f.cubin'],capture_output=True,text=True)
s=r.stdout
import re
for k in ['LDL','STL','HMMA','LDG','STG','RED','ATOMS','UBLKCP','SYNCS','BAR.SYNC','MUFU','WARPSYNC','BRA']:
    print(k, len(re.findall(r'\b'+re.escape(k), s)))

content.thinking: No register spills, but the SASS shows excess WARPSYNC relative to HMMA counts, confirming the waterfall issue from a data-dependent branch in the unroll-2 remainder check. I'll fix this by restructuring the K loop into fixed 32-wide steps with upfront fragment loads, using warp-uniform indexing via `__shfl_sync`, bulk-loading small parameters into smem, splitting the x+b2 prefill across CTAs, and unrolling slot loads.
